request.spec:
A name or alias may no longer be used on a sheet when any sheet of its tree (its ancestors, its
descendants and their descendants, among the sheets that exist) already uses it as a name or alias:
adding, renaming, an alias, the quick-add bar, the paste box (and any later import) are refused as a
duplicate would be. People who already clash are not changed: each shows clashing yes, and every
edit of them through the person form is refused until the edit renames them to a name that does not
clash (and leaves no clashing alias).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A name or alias may no longer be used on a sheet when any sheet of its tree (its ancestors, its
descendants and their descendants, among the sheets that exist) already uses it as a name or alias:
adding, renaming, an alias, the quick-add bar, the paste box (and any later import) are refused as a
duplicate would be. People who already clash are not changed: each shows clashing yes, and every
edit of them through the person form is refused until the edit renames them to a name that does not
clash (and leaves no clashing alias).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Names and aliases now have to be unique across a sheet's whole tree, not just within one sheet. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec. Before the change all 4 failed. I ran it on port 3417 (`PORT=3417 bin/e2e`) because another run on this machine was using port 3000. The background-task failure notice was just a wait loop I stopped myself.

**What's refused now.** A name or alias is refused if any other sheet in the tree already uses it as a name or alias. The tree is the sheet's ancestors (following parents, with a loop guard) plus all its descendants, limited to sheets that exist. Sibling sheets aren't part of each other's tree. Names are compared the same way as before. The check covers:
- adding a person, including through the quick-add bar;
- renaming someone in the person form;
- adding an alias.

Paste only ever finds people already on the sheet and creates no names, so it was already refused in this case. There is no import feature in the app yet.

**People who already clash.** A person clashes if their name or any of their aliases is used elsewhere in the tree. Nothing about them is changed. Every save through the person form is refused until the new name doesn't clash and none of their aliases do. Since the form can't change aliases, someone with a clashing alias can't be saved through it at all. Bulk grade goes through the same save, so it's refused for them too.

**Screen.** The person view has a new `clashing` field, and the people table has a `person-clashing` cell showing yes or no. I also added the missing "Aliases" and new "Clashing" column headers. The table was already missing the Aliases header, which put the columns out of line with their headings.

**Beyond the request:** I applied the same check to transferring a person to another sheet, ignoring the person's own name and aliases since they're the ones moving. Transfer wasn't in the request, but it's another way a name lands on a sheet. Say if you'd rather I take it out.

No database migration was needed. The changes are in `PersonService` (where the tree check lives), `PersonRepository`, `PersonAliasRepository`, `PersonController`, `TransferService` and `people.ts`.
